survey: A coral reef cluster on a flat green floor. Main parts: (1) A large pink branching coral in the centre. Its thick trunk rises from the top of a dark slate rock and splits into rounded, forked branches with dotted polyp texture. In the close-up, a front branch overlaps the trunk but grows out of it cleanly. (2) Two orange branching corals behind, one at left and one at right. Their bases are hidden behind the rocks, which reads as them growing from the same rock bed. (3) A purple/magenta branching coral in front at left. It grows up from the rocks, and its lobes overlap the pink coral's base without merging into it. (4) A small red coral at front centre, rooted in the gap between the front rocks. (5) A group of rounded grey-blue and teal rocks. They sit flat on the floor and cast contact shadows, with the large central rock acting as the base for the corals. Every coral is rooted on rock or in the rock bed, nothing floats, and the branching is organic and plausible for coral.
